etymologies.etymologyHTML: From cosmopolite +‎ -an. Compare metropolitan and megalopolitan.

definitions.definition: (of a place or institution) Composed of people from all over the world.
(of a person) At ease in any part of the world; familiar with many cultures.

quote.citation: 2013 November 25, Caroline Ferguson, “What kind of global citizens are teachers creating?”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: The philosophy of cosmopolitanism underlies theories of global citizenship. Cosmopolitanism is the ability to balance a local and global identity. A cosmopolitan individual engages meaningfully with different cultures and feels at home in the world.

definitions.definition: (biology, ecology) Growing or living in many parts of the world; widely distributed.

quote.citation: 2005, David K. Yeates, Brian M. Wiegmann, The Evolutionary Biology of Flies, page 372:
quote.text: Domestication and the evolution of anthrophilic traits in houseflies and some drosophilids have allowed certain species to attain cosmopolitan status.

quote.citation: 1934, Agatha Christie, chapter 3, in Murder on the Orient Express, London: HarperCollins, published 2017, page 25:

definitions.definition: A cocktail containing vodka, triple sec, lime juice and cranberry juice.
(Canada, US, dated) A butterfly of species Vanessa cardui.
A moth of species Leucania loreyi.
